source_refs.note: Exercise 14.2, Question 12: work done by a force of given magnitude and direction (book p.275). Answer 99 sqrt(26)/13 Nm agrees with the key (PDF 312).

blocks.prompt: 12. A force of magnitude 6 units acting parallel to \(4\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - \underline{k}\) displace the point of application from \(A(2, -1, 3)\) to \(B(7, 3, 2)\). Find the work done.
blocks.explanation:
Here the force is not given in components: we know its size (6) and its direction (parallel to \(4\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - \underline{k}\)).
Plan: build \(\underline{F}\) = magnitude times unit vector, find \(\underline{AB}\), then \(W = \underline{F}\cdot\underline{d}\).
steps:
Given: \(|\underline{F}| = 6\), \(\underline{F}\) parallel to \(\underline{u} = 4\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - \underline{k}\); the point moves from \(A(2, -1, 3)\) to \(B(7, 3, 2)\).
To find: work done.
Method: Work done by a constant force \(W = \underline{F}\cdot\underline{d}\) (14.2.8), where \(\underline{d}\) is the displacement vector from the starting point to the end point. A vector of length 6 along \(\underline{u}\) is \(6\dfrac{\underline{u}}{|\underline{u}|}\).

Unit vector along \(\underline{u}\)
\[|\underline{u}| = \sqrt{16 + 9 + 1} = \sqrt{26}\]
\[\hat{u} = \dfrac{4\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - \underline{k}}{\sqrt{26}}\]
Why: Dividing a vector by its length gives length 1 in the same direction.

The force
\[\underline{F} = 6\,\hat{u} = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{26}}(4\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - \underline{k})\]
Why: Multiplying a unit vector by 6 gives a vector of magnitude 6 in that direction.

Displacement
\[\underline{d} = (7 - 2)\underline{i} + (3 + 1)\underline{j} + (2 - 3)\underline{k}\]
\[= 5\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} - \underline{k}\]
Why: End point minus starting point.

Work done
\[W = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{26}}\,(20 + 12 + 1)\]
\[= \dfrac{198}{\sqrt{26}} = \dfrac{198\sqrt{26}}{26}\]
\[= \dfrac{99\sqrt{26}}{13}\]
Why: \((4\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - \underline{k})\cdot(5\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} - \underline{k}) = 20 + 12 + 1 = 33\); then rationalise and cancel 2.

Check
\[\dfrac{99\sqrt{26}}{13} \approx 38.8\]
\[|\underline{F}||\underline{d}| = 6\sqrt{42} \approx 38.9\]
Why: The work is just below \(|\underline{F}||\underline{d}|\), since the force is almost along the displacement (\(\cos\theta \approx 0.998\)).
